Zuko's Trust Kids

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
This is a carte Blanche investigation that doesn't let go. We take it to the next level, we don't say no-one is doing anything and thats the end of the story. We say no-one is doing anything, so we will!

Justice may never catch up with Nonxuba, but these kids will get their money!


Summary:
We recap story 1
We establish that no-one, but us, is actually investigating the fact there is a list of 12 plaintiffs whose money has been paid out by the ECDOH, yet they have never received it. Has Nonxuba stolen it? what is left in his fidelity account, which is now being curated by the LPC?

We take the list, we find the kids, confirm their stories
We prove that no-one but us is chasing this.

We confront the LPC, why are these children's trusts not being sorted out by them the curator of Nonxuba's fidelity account?
The buck stops with them
Every child we show in distress, every child dying at home in a village somewhere is now on them!

We get Gerrie Nel, who is fighting for these kids rights, to show us the anger at the LPC's incompetence and give us hope that there is another side to this.

I have to show the victims, but show the scale and no get hang up on one child.

Script:




VIZ: Masa putting mic No-Oma
Mr Nonxuba it is Masa Kekane here .....

VO 1
In April this year, we brought you our bone-chilling investigation of litigation lawyer Zuko Nonxuba.

Story 1 up sound
there's that saying to understand society, look at how it treats its kids and it's elderly
And instead of doing right by them,
He stole from them and not only from them and from the country

VO 2
An Eastern Cape attorney, Nonxuba had allegedly defrauded the state of millions by submitting fake medical negligence claims for children never born or damaged in hospital.. and stealing from his own desperately sick clients.


Story 1 up sound:
so many of these summonses were basically identical, and he wasn't even bothering to make them unique to each patient.

VO 3: Nonxuba stole from a crippled public health system, and as the evidence mounted, we went in search of some his clients, children with cerebral palsy, like 9-year-old Avile Molose.

Millicent kids coughing scene

VO 4
We met Avile and his mother, Millicent in a village near Willowvale. He was very sick. Living in abject poverty, they were unaware that the Eastern Cape Department of Health had awarded Avile 15 million Rand. … money that had already been paid over to Nonxuba as early as 2019.

Her reaction

Story 1 up sound:
The plaintiffs would tell us they got 200,000 rands or 230,000 thousand rands for their Cerebral palsy child, yet we are sitting with a court order that's awarded them 23 million or 16 million.
And these guys had no idea.

VO 5
Nonxuba, a lawyer claiming to fight for the people, was exploiting desperate children with cerebral palsy – a condition often arising from mishandled births - from the remotest and poorest parts of the former Transkei.

Story 1 up sound:
He mainly targeted those villages because he knew that theSE people are desperate

BRIDGE:
LINK: As part of our initial investigation, we obtained this audit from the Eastern Cape treasury. It details 20 cases where the Department of Health paid monies to Nonxuba, which he never paid to his clients.

VO 6
Behind each of the 20 names in this startling document was a child likely in need of care.

Our investigation would shift to the organisation responsible for oversight of the people practising law. The deeper we dug, the more questions we had for the Legal Practice Council or LPC. Were they aware of the allegations against Nonxuba, and – if they were, what action had they taken? Or, as has been alleged, was the LPC the reason he is still practising to this day?

Chapter 2

Transition

To fully piece together the impact of Nonxuba’s behaviour and the LPC’s apparent indifference, we returned to the Eastern Cape determined to find some of the other children named in the audit.

Maps

VO 7
We set off for Thsolo, a village near Mthatha, in search of No-oma Mnyimbashe.
According to the treasury audit, 16 million rands was paid out for her DAUGHTER Iviwe close to five years ago.
The court ordered Nonxuba, who was acting for her, to open a trust account in the child's name. (PAUSE)

Trusts are separate accounts overseen by trustees, aimed at keeping the beneficiary’s money safe.

It appears the account was never opened.

Hello - hello Masa Kekana

After an arduous journey, we’re told No-oma has moved to the North West in search of work. Her daughter Iviwe still lives here with her granny, but we manage to reach No-Oma by phone

Hello
Yes, I can hear you Sisi
No-oma Greeting her daughter over the phone
NO-oma:
I would love to stay with my daughter; however, due to the financial situation at home, I must go out and work
I am not happy as I do not like leaving my child. I left her because I have no other option,

Masa: When did you last yeat from Nonxuba
No-oma: I last spoke to him yesterday, enquiring about the case, and he told me that he was on the road. Today, when I tried to call him, his phone was on voicemail.

MASA: Sis, there is something I need to tell you
U’ Zuko Nonxuba he got 16 million 400 hundred thousand for your case. This money is for you and your child.

No-oma: Yo Yo … so much money …. I don’t know, I don’t know …
So much money and I didn’t even get a cent.

No-oma: I am struggling so much, and all this time, my money is being taken by people who have money.
I am sorry No-Oma,, I am sorry sisi

VO 10
It’s hard to comprehend that No-Oma is forced by circumstance to live apart from her child while Nonxuba lives the high life. Harder still to figure out why the Legal Practice Council hasn’t acted.

Vo: As our investigation intensified, we realised the LPC’s history with Nonxuba goes way back, and its failure to act has caused these families IRREPARABLE DAMAGES!

VO 11
In 2018 the Special Investigating Unit and the Eastern Cape Department of Health laid fraud complaints against Nonxuba at what was then called the Law Society - now the LPC. But, because he was also facing a criminal trial, they refused to investigate. Our investigation shows Nonxuba continued winning multi-million Rand suits in that time – money that he allegedly kept for himself.

In 2019 the High Court ordered the LPC to investigate the complaints, and a year later, they released a damming report finding Nonxuba had violated numerous codes of conduct. But, again, there were no consequences.

[TRANSITION]

VO 12
Next on our list was Thandiswa Xhanti. We make us over the mountain to a village near Ngobo where she lives with her son Aluhmile. Soon after his birth Aluhmile started having seizures and was later diagnosed with Cerebral palsy.

I won’t even lie; it was painful. I had a hard time accepting his situation as I was young.

In 2020 Nonxuba told the family they’d been awarded money but never confirmed how much. According to Aluhmile’s granny Nozuko Nqunqani they were given a few thousand rands a month.

He told me to call when the baby was sick or needed food, and I would call him, and he would give me R1000.

VO 16
Three years later, the family hears for the first time that Ahlumile has been awarded 13 million rand. Thandiswa is heartbroken.
 
Thandiswa crying
granny: He uses children in this condition. He is a thief who is making himself rich.

VO 17
With a heavy heart, we leave this family behind for now, but again if all this evidence was given to the LPC back in 2021, why do none of these families know about any investigation?! When we approached the LPC for clarity, they declined to comment.

VO 18 – time lapse
Our journey continues late into the night - one family leading us to the next… the number of Nonxuba’s alleged victims is growing beyond what we could have imagined.

MASA LINK FROM THE CAR AT NIGHT
We have Crisscrossed the EC, trying to find Nonxuba’s victims and even found people that don’t even live here anymore.

AF: He promised that there would be funds for the child, but how much, I don’t know.
Masa: He owes you 21 million.
AF: I have never received such an amount.

VO 19
Almost 5 years ago, Nonxuba was paid over 21 million for Andiswa Fitshane's son Sinesipho.

AFi: Each month, he gives me R5000, but if I say it is not enough, he tells me that I love money too much

VO 20
It’s hard to imagine a more callous response… ridiculing Andiswa, while apparently pocketing the 21 million owed to her son.

Masa: Have the police or anybody contacted you about this case,
AF: No

VO 21
With such overwhelming evidence, how could it be that no one was investigating these missing trusts? As we joined the dots, we discovered that the Eastern Cape’s Treasury Department did open a criminal case with the police's commercial crimes unit two years ago, but the docket lay dormant until our first story aired in April. According to a source, the case is now receiving attention.

But it’s two years too late for these children.

VO 22
Yandiswa Feni’s son Akahluwa is nine years old but looks like a toddler. A lack of treatment for cerebral palsy is causing severe muscle spasms and affecting his bone density.

YF: He can not hold anything, his arms are always like this, as you can see.
His hands are always stiff like this. If I try to stretch him, I can see he is in pain.
It becomes difficult to feed him; he eats bit by bit.
and sometimes he vomits
He has a tiny body

VO 23
Underweight and desperate for medical treatment, Akahluwa is trapped here, without the money needed to see a doctor.

YF: It was in 2019, the last time I took him to the doctor, and he had asthma

VO 24
Just like every other family we speak to on this journey, Yandiswa is unaware her child was awarded 22 million rand - paid to Nonxuba about four years ago.
intoni?What?
Haybo!( shocked )
It is painful, so painful.

Our children can get the help that they need and deserve, as there is nothing we can do without money.
And this money has been kept away from us

VO 25
After years of failing to hold Nonxuba accountable, the LPC - under pressure from the Eastern Cape Department of Health, did manage to suspended him last year. But, he’s challenging the move in the Constitutional Court so, for now, remains a practising attorney.

[TRANSITION]

VO 26
After watching our first story and heartbroken by what he saw, Johannesburg lawyer, Armand Du Plessis, flew to the Eastern Cape to take on Millicent Molose’s case. Unable to reach Nonxuba, he contacted the LPC for an answer about Avile Molose’s missing 13 million rand.

Armand
The Legal Practice Council confirmed that they have taken control of the trust account of this particular attorney and are busy administrating it.

VO 27
Legal practitioners are required to hold Fidelity Fund Certificates because they take deposits from clients and operate trust accounts. But, because of his suspension, Nonxuba’s fidelity trust account is now under the LPC’s management. (PAUSE)

But at the time of this broadcast, nearly two months after first contacting them, the LPC still has no answer to Armand’s questions about Avile’s missing millions.

VO 28
LINK: Again we tried to persuade the LPC to speak to us. They responded in writing saying that only once Nonxuba’s suspension case was finalised would they be able to engage with us and “assist all persons affected by this matter.”

A date for this hearing has yet to be set.

Yandiswa Feni: I wish Mr Nonxuba could be arrested, arrested for everyone
that he has hurt people who feel the same hurt AS ME

VO 29
During our first story, desperate for answers, we tried to track Nonxuba down but his officers were permanently closed, and none of the numbers we had were working.

A few days after we returned from the Eastern Cape No-Oma called to say she had asked Nonxuba about her child's money, and he wanted to meet with her. We knew this was our chance to confront him, finally

Where are you now – masa walks out

But Nonxuba cancelled their meeting numerous times, so we travelled to Rustenburg to get No-Oma to call him on camera.

From off-camera, we tell No-Oma to push for an in-person meeting, as she needs answers.


Nonxuba never answered our calls again...
All we can do now is hope that this time around, the wheels of justice do something to get these children their money before its too late.
